newsitem.title: UK: UK Treasury minister summons pensions chiefs.
newsitem.headline: UK Treasury minister summons pensions chiefs.

text.p: Economic Secretary to the Treasury Helen Liddell has summoned senior officials of large companies involved in the personal pensions business to a meeting on Wednesday, a Treasury statement said.
It said Liddell would use the meeting "to let the industry know the Government's thinking on the review of personal pensions".
The Treasury added that it would issue a statement following the 1500 gmt meeting.

British newspapers speculated that Liddell would put pressure on the firms to produce convincing plans to compensate victims of personal pensions mis-selling, saying she will "name and shame" the worst offenders unless this is done.
Thousands of Britons sold a personal pension in the late 1980s and early 1990s lost out by leaving more lucrative occupational pension schemes.

The Labour Party said in its manifesto for the May 1 election it would reform the Financial Services Act "so that the scandal of pensions mis-selling -- 600,000 pensions mis-sold and only 7,000 people compensated to date -- will not happen again". -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
